answer: Requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake bond before it can earn makes fake identities expensive: one bond buys one voice, and slashing burns the bond if the agent cheats. Like a cedar that only grows where its roots are planted, an identity must be anchored to real collateral rather than floating free. A sybil swarm then looks like a plume of smoke, wide but weightless, while honest agents keep a haven of earned reputation that no cheap copy can inherit.
